prediction.likelyOutcome: EQY should recover close to the full $170,484.37 in past-due rent it has pled, since Williamson's mitigation and personal-property offset theories are evidentiarily thin (no proof of an earlier reletting opportunity, no quantified build-out value, no request to retrieve the property). Expect the court to reject most or all of the requested offsets, award attorney's fees under Rohrmoos-compliant proof, and hold Gore jointly liable on the guaranty.

issues.label: Unpaid Rent Under the Lease (Aug. 2023 - Dec. 21, 2024)

figures.label: Past-due rent, Aug. 1, 2023 - Dec. 21, 2024
figures.quote: damages of $170,484.37 representing past-due rent owed under the Lease from August 1, 2023, through December 21, 2024, the overlap of the remainder of Williamson's lease and Hallmark's lease term

figures.label: Claimed overlap-period rent/interest offset
figures.quote: Williamson sought an offset for the rent and interest EQY claimed for months that overlapped with Hallmark's lease term, calculated at $62,096.52.

figures.label: Claimed value of retained furniture/equipment
figures.quote: Williamson also complains that EQY's damages should be reduced by $20,000.00 to account for the value of Williamson's personal property remaining on the premises when EQY locked Williamson out for non-payment of rent.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the court awarded the landlord $170,484.37 in past-due rent, the full amount it sought, with no credit for the $62,096.52 free-rent overlap offset or the $20,000 personal property. It also awarded $86,725.00 in attorney's fees. On appeal the rent damages were affirmed and the fee award reversed.
outcome.finalNote: Rent damages affirmed; fee award reversed.
